title: LSASS memory access with full-access masks by PowerShell on scranton and wsmprovhost on nashua
rationale: All these findings describe the same action: PowerShell.exe (PID 2976) on scranton opened lsass.exe with 0x1f3fff/0x1fffff at 03:05:16Z, and wsmprovhost.exe on nashua opened lsass.exe with 0x1f3fff at 03:09:29Z. The full-access handle to LSASS memory is the classic credential-dumping pattern, best mapped to T1003.001 (LSASS Memory).

title: Keylogging and clipboard capture on scranton
rationale: pbeesly ran Get-Keystrokes with a Keystrokes job and read the clipboard. The primary input-capture action is keylogging (T1056.001).

title: Forced authentication via WebDAV/UNC coercion from scranton to 192.168.0.4
rationale: SMB attempts to 192.168.0.4 were rejected, then WebDAV requests with Microsoft-WebDAV-MiniRedir were issued and answered 401 — coercion of authentication to an attacker-controlled server, matching T1187 (Forced Authentication).

title: Hidden PowerShell stager opened Microsoft Edge processes with PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS
rationale: A hidden, execution-policy-bypassing PowerShell stager decoded a payload from monkey.png and opened Edge processes with 0x1fffff, consistent with in-memory browser session-cookie theft (T1539).

title: Unsecured credentials staged and exfiltrated via Invoke-Exfil on scranton
rationale: Invoke-Exfil compressed the Downloads directory (holding exported .pfx) into OfficeSupplies.7z and copied it to \\192.168.0.4\webdav using hardcoded credentials; PsExec also used cleartext password. The credential-access element is unsecured credentials (T1552).

title: Credential-hunting file collection and plaintext credential use
rationale: pbeesly recursively enumerated the user profile for credential-bearing file patterns and archived them into working.zip, then Rar'd and sdelete'd them; also used plaintext passwords. The credential-access action is credentials in files (T1552.001).

title: Get-PrivateKeys exported LocalMachine certificate private keys to .pfx on scranton
rationale: All describe the same script block (Get-PrivateKeys, readme.ps1) enumerating cert:\LocalMachine and calling Export-PfxCertificate to write .pfx files protected by hardcoded password 'saribas'. This is private-key theft, T1552.004.

title: Credential/certificate theft tooling staged on scranton with no web-credential forging observed
rationale: Get-PrivateKeys exported certificate private keys and LSASS was accessed; the theft of authentication certificates maps to T1649 (Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates).

title: Low-confidence hostui.exe and sdclt.exe process anomalies on scranton
rationale: hostui.exe spawned by PowerShell and sdclt.exe spawned by cmd are process-execution anomalies (sdclt is UAC-bypass-capable), not observed credential access. Out-of-scope (T1036/T1548).

title: Attacker python.exe on nashua as C2/exfil client
rationale: The dropped python.exe unpacks a PyInstaller bundle and makes hundreds of outbound connections to 192.168.0.4:8443 — C2/exfiltration traffic, not network sniffing. Out-of-scope (T1071).

title: Sysinternals credential-access toolchain, PsExec lateral movement and anti-forensic cleanup by pbeesly
rationale: These findings cover staging of SysinternalsSuite, accesschk, PsExec64 with cleartext credentials against NASHUA, and sdelete64 wiping artifacts. The core observed action is lateral movement/execution via PsExec, not credential access, so it is out-of-scope (T1569).
